column1: # Assemblies for the cross-species re-test. One row per reference.
# species  label  era  fasta_url  gtf_url
# `era` is the column the experiment turns on: `old` is the assembly the 2014
# paper had, `new` is the best available today. Every species contributes one
# of each, so the reference axis is a paired comparison within species.
# Sources are UCSC throughout, and deliberately not NCBI: NCBI's *_genomic.fna.gz
# is soft-masked with WindowMasker rather than RepeatMasker, and for opossum and
# fly it ships no RepeatMasker product at all. Mixing a WindowMasker FASTA with a
# RepeatMasker annotation is a silent inconsistency in a study whose signal is
# about repeats.
# Note which URL the 2026 opossum lives at. UCSC's named `monDom5` browser and
# Ensembl's ASM229v1 are both still the 2006 genome; mMonDom1.pri is reachable
# only through GenArk or NCBI Datasets. Taking the obvious path re-runs the 2014
# experiment on the 2014 reference without announcing it.
# Chromosome naming differs by source and is checked at prep time rather than
# assumed: GenArk assemblies name sequences by RefSeq accession (NC_077227.1),
# goldenPath assemblies use chr1..chrX. A GTF whose names do not intersect its
# FASTA's is a hard error, not a warning -- it would otherwise produce an empty
# junction list and a silently degraded HISAT2 arm.
#species
opossum
opossum
# Rows below are the rest of the panel, not run by the pilot. Uncomment to extend.
# Rat is the largest assembly improvement of any species here (contig N50 52 kb
# -> 64 Mb, 1,224x) and therefore the largest predicted effect after opossum.
#rat
#rat
#mouse
#mouse
# Fly is the negative control: dm6's contig N50 is byte-identical to dm3's, so
# the assembly axis is null for it by construction. If the other species move
# and fly does not, the movement is assembly-driven. Both arms cost ~40 min.
#fly
